newsitem.title: UK: Moody's rates Aon, unit securities, may cut.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates Aon, unit securities, may cut.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it assigned an A3 rating to the $800 million of Capital Securities of Aon Capital Trust A, as well as assigning a Baa1 rating to the related junior subordinated debentures issued by Aon Corporation to Aon Capital Trust A.
"These ratings were simultaneously placed under review for possible downgrade," Moody's said in a statement.

Moody's also reiterated its review for downgrade of its other ratings on the securities of Aon Corporation, including the A2 rating on Aon's senior long-term debt, the A3 rating on Aon's preferred stock, and the Prime-1 rating for commercial paper.

"The Capital Securities were sold in a private placement offering to qualified institutional buyers under SEC Rule 144A; in turn, the net proceeds will be used to acquire designated junior subordinated debentures issued by Aon Corporation," Moody's said.
"Aon intends to use the proceeds from the sale of the junior subordinated debentures to help finance Aon's acquisition of Alexander & Alexander Services Inc (A&A) in a $1.23 billion transaction."

The agency said its review, initiated by Aon's announced acquisition of A&A in December 1996, would continue to focus on the strategic benefits Aon may be able to garner from an acquisition of A&A, as well as the firm's future acquisition appetite. Several months ago, Aon acquired the Bain Hogg Group, a London-based insurance broker with a strong presence in Europe and in various specialty commercial lines.

"Moody's will also review the developing competitive environment of the global insurance brokerage business, and Aon's plans to position itself in that environment. Furthermore, Moody's will examine the financial implications of the A&A acquisition, in addition to Aon's long-term capital structure plans," Moody's said.
